answer: A practical defense is a per-agent stake locked before it can earn from the grove: the protocol randomly assigns work, then slashes stake when independently checked outputs fail a challenge. One operator can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital, and each failed identity risks losing it; splitting a stake across aliases does not multiply the total weight. A quill may submit a claim from the terrace, yet it earns no trust merely by appearing under a new name.
